## 🎯 What It Does
This is the "Edit" page of the wiki app — a quality-control dashboard that surfaces problems in the knowledge base (orphan pages, stale claims, missing concepts, contradictions, promotion candidates) and lets the user fix, dismiss, promote, or research each issue with one click.

## ⚙️ How It Works
- Runs a "lint pass" on the active project that scans the wiki for issues, then displays findings grouped by category (contradictions, orphans, missing concepts, etc.)
- Each finding shows contextual action buttons — auto-fixable issues get a "Fix" button, child-page findings get "Promote to parent," gaps get "Research," and recurring themes get "Create concept"
- Supports bulk "Fix all" for categories where multiple items can be repaired at once, with automatic polling until the job completes
- Filters findings by status (active / dismissed / resolved / all) and remembers which category groups are collapsed

## 🔗 What It Connects To
- **Project switcher** — scopes every action to the currently active project
- **Lint API** (`/api/lint/*`) for running passes, fixing findings, and dismissing
- **Promote / Concept-scaffold / Research APIs** — hands work off to other parts of the app
- **Sources page** for research hand-off and **Wiki page** for opening target pages
- **Toast system** for success/error feedback and **Dispatch/Jobs** for tracking queued fixes

## 📊 Key Details
- Five categories are auto-fixable; the rest (suggested questions, promotion candidates, themes, gaps) need a human decision
- Optimistically shows a "running" state immediately on lint start to avoid a race where the UI misses the new job
- Supports a `?run=1` URL shortcut so the command palette can trigger a lint pass on arrival
- Uses fade-out animations (`gone` state) when items are dismissed or resolved, so the list doesn't jump abruptly
